subject: Corporate and Economic Laws
topicTitle: SEBI Act and key SEBI regulations
tag: [ICAI CA Final PYQ] Sec 11B - Power of SEBI to Issue Directions & Impound Proceeds
question: Under Section 11B of the Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI) Act, 1992, which of the following measures can SEBI direct against an intermediary or market participant in the interests of investors or orderly market development?
options: Suspend the trading of any security in a recognized stock exchange, restrain persons from accessing the securities market, and direct impounding and retention of all proceeds or securities involved in the violation.
Direct the compulsory dissolution of the corporate entity without reference to NCLT.
Cancel the Indian passport of the company's directors.
Order military custody of the company's premises.
ref: Section 11(4) and Section 11B of the SEBI Act, 1992
explanation: Under Section 11(4) and 11B, SEBI has comprehensive powers to issue directions including: (a) suspending trading of any security; (b) restraining persons from accessing the securities market; (c) impounding and retaining proceeds; and (d) directing attachment of bank accounts for up to 90 days.

subject: Corporate and Economic Laws
topicTitle: SEBI Act and key SEBI regulations
tag: [ICAI CA Final PYQ] Sec 15G - Penalty for Insider Trading
question: An insider of a listed entity trades in the securities of the company on the basis of Unpublished Price Sensitive Information (UPSI) and earns unlawful profits of ₹8 Crores. Under Section 15G of the SEBI Act, 1992, what is the maximum monetary penalty that can be imposed by the Adjudicating Officer?
options: A penalty which shall not be less than ₹10 Lakhs, but which may extend to ₹25 Crores or three times the amount of profits made out of insider trading, whichever is higher (i.e. up to ₹25 Crores or ₹24 Crores -> max ₹25 Crores).
Fixed penalty of ₹1 Crore only.
A penalty strictly capped at double the investment value.
Fine up to ₹50 Lakhs with mandatory 7 years imprisonment.
ref: Section 15G of the Securities and Exchange Board of India Act, 1992
explanation: Under Section 15G, if any insider deals in securities on the basis of UPSI or communicates UPSI, he shall be liable to a penalty which shall not be less than ten lakh rupees, but which may extend to twenty-five crore rupees or three times the amount of profits made out of insider trading, whichever is higher.

subject: Corporate and Economic Laws
topicTitle: SEBI Act and key SEBI regulations
tag: [ICAI CA Final PYQ] Sec 15T & 15Z - Appeal to SAT and Supreme Court
question: An order imposing a monetary penalty is passed by the Adjudicating Officer of SEBI on May 2. By what date must the aggrieved entity file an appeal before the Securities Appellate Tribunal (SAT) under Section 15T, and within what period may an appeal against SAT order be filed to the Supreme Court under Section 15Z?
options: Appeal to SAT within 45 days from the date of receipt of copy of order; Appeal against SAT order to Supreme Court on question of law within 60 days from communication of order.
Appeal to SAT within 30 days; Appeal to Supreme Court within 30 days.
Appeal to SAT within 60 days; Appeal to Supreme Court within 90 days.
Appeal to SAT within 15 days; Appeal to High Court within 30 days.
ref: Section 15T(3) and Section 15Z of the SEBI Act, 1992
explanation: Under Section 15T(3), every appeal to the Securities Appellate Tribunal shall be filed within a period of 45 days from the date on which a copy of the order is received. Under Section 15Z, any person aggrieved by any decision or order of the Securities Appellate Tribunal may file an appeal to the Supreme Court for any question of law arising out of such order within 60 days from the date of communication.

subject: Corporate and Economic Laws
topicTitle: SEBI Act and key SEBI regulations
tag: [ICAI CA Final PYQ] SEBI (LODR) Reg 17 - Board Composition & Independent Directors
question: Under Regulation 17(1) of SEBI (Listing Obligations and Disclosure Requirements) Regulations, 2015, if the Chairperson of the Board of Directors of a listed entity is a non-executive director and is a promoter or related to any promoter, what proportion of the Board must comprise Independent Directors?
options: At least half (50%) of the Board of Directors shall consist of Independent Directors.
At least one-third (33.33%) of the Board of Directors.
At least two-thirds (66.67%) of the Board of Directors.
Only 2 independent directors are required regardless of promoter relation.
ref: Regulation 17(1)(b) proviso of SEBI (LODR) Regulations, 2015
explanation: Under Regulation 17(1)(b), where the chairperson of the board of directors is a non-executive director, at least one-third of the board of directors shall comprise of independent directors. However, under the proviso, where the non-executive chairperson is a promoter of the listed entity or is related to any promoter or person occupying management positions, at least half (50%) of the board of directors shall consist of independent directors.

subject: Corporate and Economic Laws
topicTitle: SEBI Act and key SEBI regulations
tag: [ICAI CA Final PYQ] SEBI (LODR) Reg 18 - Audit Committee Composition & Quorum
question: Under Regulation 18 of SEBI (LODR) Regulations, 2015, which of the following requirements regarding the Audit Committee of a listed entity is MANDATORY?
options: The Audit Committee shall have minimum 3 directors as members, at least two-thirds of the members shall be independent directors, and the Chairperson shall be an independent director who shall be present at AGM.
All members of the Audit Committee must be executive directors with accounting degrees.
Audit Committee quorum is one director personally present.
Audit Committee is required to meet only once every financial year.
ref: Regulation 18(1) and 18(2) of SEBI (LODR) Regulations, 2015
explanation: Under Regulation 18(1), the Audit Committee must have minimum 3 directors, at least two-thirds of the members shall be independent directors (for listed entities with SR equity shares, all members must be independent), and the Chairperson shall be an independent director present at the AGM. Quorum is two members or one-third, whichever is greater, with at least two independent directors.

subject: Corporate and Economic Laws
topicTitle: SEBI Act and key SEBI regulations
tag: [ICAI CA Final PYQ] SEBI (LODR) Reg 23 - Material Related Party Transactions (RPT)
question: Under Regulation 23 of SEBI (LODR) Regulations, 2015, a transaction with a related party shall be considered 'material' if the transaction(s) to be entered into individually or taken together with previous transactions during a financial year exceeds which threshold?
options: ₹1,000 Crore OR 10% of the annual consolidated turnover of the listed entity as per the last audited financial statements, whichever is lower.
₹100 Crore or 5% of turnover, whichever is higher.
10% of net worth of the holding company exclusively.
₹500 Crore regardless of consolidated turnover.
ref: Regulation 23(1) of SEBI (LODR) Regulations, 2015 (as amended)
explanation: Under amended Regulation 23(1), a transaction with a related party shall be considered material if the transaction(s) to be entered into individually or taken together with previous transactions during a financial year, exceeds ₹1,000 Crore or 10% of the annual consolidated turnover of the listed entity as per the last audited financial statements, whichever is lower. Prior shareholder approval by ordinary resolution is required.

subject: Corporate and Economic Laws
topicTitle: SEBI Act and key SEBI regulations
tag: [ICAI CA Final PYQ] SEBI (LODR) Reg 30 - Disclosure of Material Events to Stock Exchanges
question: A listed pharmaceutical company discovers an unexpected fire accident causing severe damage of ₹60 Crores to its active pharmaceutical ingredient manufacturing unit. Under Regulation 30 read with Schedule III of SEBI (LODR) Regulations, 2015, within what timeframe must the listed entity disclose this material event to stock exchanges?
options: As soon as reasonably possible and not later than 24 hours from the occurrence of the event (or 12 hours if originating from within the company).
Within 7 days of completion of the insurance surveyor's assessment.
At the immediate next quarterly financial results announcement.
Within 48 hours of Board approval of the restoration plan.
ref: Regulation 30(6) of SEBI (LODR) Regulations, 2015 (as amended in 2023)
explanation: Under Regulation 30(6) as amended, the listed entity shall disclose to the stock exchange(s) all material events as soon as reasonably possible and in any case not later than: (i) 30 minutes from closure of Board meeting for decisions; (ii) 12 hours from occurrence if originating from within; (iii) 24 hours from occurrence if not originating from within.

subject: Corporate and Economic Laws
topicTitle: SEBI Act and key SEBI regulations
tag: [ICAI CA Final PYQ] SEBI (PIT) Reg 2(1)(n) - Unpublished Price Sensitive Information (UPSI)
question: Under Regulation 2(1)(n) of SEBI (Prohibition of Insider Trading) Regulations, 2015, which of the following is explicitly deemed to be Unpublished Price Sensitive Information (UPSI)?
options: Financial results, dividends, change in capital structure, mergers, de-mergers, acquisitions, delistings, disposals and expansion of business, and changes in Key Managerial Personnel.
Routine quarterly sales volume disclosures published on company website.
Public press releases announcing award of industry excellence trophies.
Employee retirement notices below managerial cadre.
ref: Regulation 2(1)(n) of SEBI (Prohibition of Insider Trading) Regulations, 2015
explanation: Under Regulation 2(1)(n), 'unpublished price sensitive information' means any information, relating to a company or its securities, directly or indirectly, that is not generally available which upon becoming generally available is likely to materially affect the price of securities, including: financial results, dividends, change in capital structure, M&A/restructuring, and changes in KMP.

subject: Corporate and Economic Laws
topicTitle: SEBI Act and key SEBI regulations
tag: [ICAI CA Final PYQ] SEBI (PIT) Reg 9 - Trading Window Closure Period
question: Under Clause 4 of Schedule B read with Regulation 9 of SEBI (PIT) Regulations, 2015, trading window restrictions shall mandatorily be applied by listed entities from which date until when?
options: From the end of every quarter till 48 hours after the declaration of financial results.
From 7 days before the Board meeting till 24 hours after results declaration.
Only on the exact day of the Board meeting approving financial statements.
From the beginning of the financial year till the Annual General Meeting.
ref: Clause 4 of Schedule B of SEBI (Prohibition of Insider Trading) Regulations, 2015
explanation: Under Clause 4 of Schedule B (Minimum Standards for Code of Conduct), trading restriction period shall be made applicable from the end of every quarter till 48 hours after the declaration of financial results. Designated persons and their immediate relatives are prohibited from trading during this window closure.

subject: Corporate and Economic Laws
topicTitle: SEBI Act and key SEBI regulations
tag: [ICAI CA Final PYQ] SEBI (SAST) Reg 3 - Substantial Acquisition Threshold (Trigger Limit)
question: Under Regulation 3(1) of SEBI (Substantial Acquisition of Shares and Takeovers) Regulations, 2011 (SAST), what is the threshold of voting rights that triggers the mandatory obligation to make a public announcement of an open offer to acquire shares from public shareholders?
options: Acquiring shares or voting rights which taken together with existing holdings entitle the acquirer and PACs to exercise 25% or more of voting rights in the target company.
Acquiring 15% or more of voting rights.
Acquiring 51% or more of paid-up equity share capital.
Acquiring any voting rights exceeding 5% in a single financial year.
ref: Regulation 3(1) of SEBI (SAST) Regulations, 2011
explanation: Under Regulation 3(1) of SEBI (SAST) Regulations, no acquirer shall acquire shares or voting rights in a target company which taken together with shares or voting rights held by him and by persons acting in concert (PAC) with him in such target company, entitle them to exercise twenty-five per cent (25%) or more of the voting rights, unless the acquirer makes a public announcement of an open offer.

subject: Corporate and Economic Laws
topicTitle: SEBI Act and key SEBI regulations
tag: [ICAI CA Final PYQ] SEBI (SAST) Reg 3(2) - Creeping Acquisition Limit
question: An acquirer holds 38% voting rights in an equity listed company. During FY 2024-25, the acquirer desires to purchase additional shares from the open market without triggering a mandatory open offer. What is the maximum percentage of voting rights the acquirer can acquire under the 'creeping acquisition' provision of Regulation 3(2)?
options: Up to 5% of voting rights in that financial year, provided the acquisition does not result in total holding exceeding maximum permissible non-public shareholding (75%).
Up to 10% of voting rights in any financial year.
Up to 2% of voting rights every quarter.
Zero additional shares can be acquired without an open offer once holding exceeds 25%.
ref: Regulation 3(2) of SEBI (SAST) Regulations, 2011
explanation: Under Regulation 3(2), an acquirer who holds 25% or more but less than maximum permissible non-public shareholding (75%) may acquire additional shares or voting rights entitling him to exercise more than 5% of voting rights in any financial year only by making an open offer. Therefore, acquisitions up to 5% in a financial year (creeping acquisition) are permitted without an open offer.

subject: Corporate and Economic Laws
topicTitle: SEBI Act and key SEBI regulations
tag: [ICAI CA Final PYQ] SEBI (SAST) Reg 7 - Offer Size in Open Offer
question: Under Regulation 7(1) of SEBI (SAST) Regulations, 2011, what is the mandatory minimum offer size that an acquirer must make in a public announcement of an open offer under Regulation 3 or Regulation 4?
options: At least twenty-six percent (26%) of total shares of the target company as of tenth working day from the closure of the tendering period.
Exactly twenty percent (20%) of the paid-up share capital.
Fifty-one percent (51%) of total voting shares.
Ten percent (10%) of the public shareholding.
ref: Regulation 7(1) of SEBI (SAST) Regulations, 2011
explanation: Under Regulation 7(1), the open offer for acquiring shares to be made by the acquirer and PAC under regulation 3 and regulation 4 shall be for at least twenty-six per cent (26%) of total shares of the target company, as of tenth working day from closure of the tendering period.

subject: Corporate and Economic Laws
topicTitle: SEBI Act and key SEBI regulations
tag: [ICAI CA Final PYQ] SEBI (ICDR) Reg 6 - Eligibility Requirements for IPO
question: An unlisted company planning an Initial Public Offering (IPO) of equity shares must satisfy which financial criteria under Regulation 6(1) of SEBI (Issue of Capital and Disclosure Requirements) Regulations, 2018?
options: Net tangible assets of at least ₹3 Cr in each of preceding 3 full years; Average operating profit of at least ₹15 Cr during preceding 3 years; Net worth of at least ₹1 Cr in each of preceding 3 full years.
Net tangible assets of at least ₹10 Cr and turnover of ₹100 Cr in the immediately preceding year.
Net profit of at least ₹50 Cr in the current year regardless of past history.
Continuous dividend payment for 10 consecutive years.
ref: Regulation 6(1) of SEBI (ICDR) Regulations, 2018
explanation: Under Regulation 6(1) (Profitability Route), the issuer must have: (a) Net tangible assets of at least ₹3 Crores in each of the preceding 3 full years (max 50% monetary assets); (b) Average operating profit of at least ₹15 Crores during the 3 most profitable years out of preceding 5 years; (c) Net worth of at least ₹1 Crore in each of the preceding 3 full years.

subject: Corporate and Economic Laws
topicTitle: SEBI Act and key SEBI regulations
tag: [ICAI CA Final PYQ] SEBI (ICDR) Reg 6(2) - QIB Book-Building Alternative Route
question: An issuer company not satisfying the profitability track record under Regulation 6(1) can still undertake an IPO of equity shares under Regulation 6(2) of SEBI (ICDR) Regulations, 2018 provided it complies with which condition?
options: The issue is made through the book-building process and the issuer undertakes to allot at least 75% of the net offer to Qualified Institutional Buyers (QIBs), and refund full subscription if minimum QIB allotment is not met.
The issue is made exclusively to retail individual investors with 50% discount.
The issuer obtains an unconditional guarantee from the Reserve Bank of India.
All directors deposit 100% of their personal assets in an escrow account with SEBI.
ref: Regulation 6(2) of SEBI (ICDR) Regulations, 2018
explanation: Under Regulation 6(2), an issuer not satisfying the conditions of Regulation 6(1) shall be eligible to make an initial public offer only if the issue is made through the book-building process and the issuer undertakes to allot, at least seventy-five per cent (75%) of the net offer to Qualified Institutional Buyers (QIBs) and to refund the full subscription money if it fails to make the said minimum allotment.

subject: Corporate and Economic Laws
topicTitle: SEBI Act and key SEBI regulations
tag: [ICAI CA Final PYQ] SEBI (ICDR) Reg 14 & 16 - Minimum Promoters Contribution & Lock-in
question: In an Initial Public Offering (IPO) of equity shares, what is the mandatory minimum promoters' contribution required, and what is the lock-in period under Regulation 14 and 16 of SEBI (ICDR) Regulations, 2018?
options: Promoters shall contribute not less than 20% of post-issue capital, locked in for 18 months (or 3 years if project involves capital expenditure), and excess promoters' holding locked in for 6 months.
Promoters must hold 51% post-issue capital locked in for 5 years.
Promoters must contribute 10% locked in for 1 year.
No lock-in applies if shares are held in dematerialized format.
ref: Regulation 14 and Regulation 16 of SEBI (ICDR) Regulations, 2018 (as amended)
explanation: Under Regulation 14, minimum promoters' contribution shall not be less than 20% of post-issue capital. Under amended Regulation 16, minimum promoters' contribution is locked in for 18 months from date of allotment (reduced from 3 years for eligible issuers), and any excess promoter shareholding is locked in for 6 months (reduced from 1 year).

subject: Corporate and Economic Laws
topicTitle: SEBI Act and key SEBI regulations
tag: [ICAI CA Final PYQ] SEBI (PIT) Reg 3 - Communication of UPSI & Legitimate Purpose
question: Under Regulation 3(2A) of SEBI (Prohibition of Insider Trading) Regulations, 2015, communicating unpublished price sensitive information (UPSI) in furtherance of 'legitimate purposes' is legally permitted. How must the Board of Directors define 'legitimate purpose'?
options: The Board shall formulate a policy for determination of 'legitimate purposes' as part of Codes of Fair Disclosure, which shall include sharing of UPSI in ordinary course of business by an insider with partners, collaborators, lenders, customers, suppliers, merchant bankers, legal advisors, auditors, or insolvency professionals.
Legitimate purpose is defined exclusively by SEBI on a case-to-case basis via formal no-objection letters.
Sharing UPSI is never permitted under any circumstance, even with statutory auditors.
Sharing UPSI is legitimate only when done via televised news interviews.
ref: Regulation 3(2A) of SEBI (Prohibition of Insider Trading) Regulations, 2015
explanation: Under Regulation 3(2A), the board of directors of a listed company shall formulate a policy for determination of 'legitimate purposes' as a part of the codes of fair disclosure. It shall include sharing of UPSI in the ordinary course of business with collaborators, lenders, customers, suppliers, merchant bankers, legal advisors, auditors, or insolvency professionals, provided sharing is not done to evade PIT prohibitions.

subject: Corporate and Economic Laws
topicTitle: SEBI Act and key SEBI regulations
tag: [ICAI CA Final PYQ] SEBI (LODR) Reg 27 - Quarterly Corporate Governance Compliance Report
question: Under Regulation 27(2) of SEBI (LODR) Regulations, 2015, within how many days from the end of each quarter must a listed entity submit a quarterly corporate governance compliance report to the recognized stock exchange(s)?
options: Within 21 days from the end of each quarter.
Within 15 days from the end of each quarter.
Within 45 days along with financial results.
Within 30 days from the closure of the quarter.
ref: Regulation 27(2)(a) of SEBI (LODR) Regulations, 2015
explanation: Under Regulation 27(2)(a), the listed entity shall submit a quarterly compliance report on corporate governance in the format as specified by the Board from time to time to the recognized stock exchange(s) within twenty-one (21) days from the end of each quarter.

subject: Corporate and Economic Laws
topicTitle: SEBI Act and key SEBI regulations
tag: [ICAI CA Final PYQ] Sec 15A - Penalty for Failure to Furnish Information/Returns
question: If any person who is required under the SEBI Act or rules to furnish any document, return or report to SEBI fails to furnish the same, what penalty is leviable under Section 15A(a)?
options: A penalty which shall not be less than ₹1 Lakh, but which may extend to ₹1 Lakh for each day during which such failure continues, subject to a maximum of ₹1 Crore.
Fixed penalty of ₹50,000 per violation.
Suspension of trading in shares for 3 years.
Immediate imprisonment for 6 months.
ref: Section 15A(a) of the Securities and Exchange Board of India Act, 1992
explanation: Under Section 15A(a), if any person fails to furnish any document, return or report to the Board, he shall be liable to a penalty which shall not be less than one lakh rupees, but which may extend to one lakh rupees for each day during which such failure continues subject to a maximum of one crore rupees.

subject: Corporate and Economic Laws
topicTitle: SEBI Act and key SEBI regulations
tag: [ICAI CA Final PYQ] SEBI (LODR) Reg 19 - Nomination & Remuneration Committee
question: Under Regulation 19 of SEBI (LODR) Regulations, 2015, what is the mandatory composition of the Nomination and Remuneration Committee for a listed entity?
options: The committee shall comprise of at least 3 directors, all directors of the committee shall be non-executive directors, and at least two-thirds of the directors shall be independent directors.
The committee must consist of 5 directors including the Chief Executive Officer.
Only executive directors can form the Nomination and Remuneration Committee.
At least half the committee must be independent directors.
ref: Regulation 19(1) of SEBI (LODR) Regulations, 2015 (as amended)
explanation: Under Regulation 19(1) of SEBI (LODR), the Nomination and Remuneration Committee shall: (a) comprise of at least three directors; (b) all directors of the committee shall be non-executive directors; (c) at least two-thirds of the directors shall be independent directors; and (d) Chairperson of the committee shall be an independent director.

subject: Corporate and Economic Laws
topicTitle: SEBI Act and key SEBI regulations
tag: [ICAI CA Final PYQ] Sec 24 - Offences & Penal Provisions by Courts
question: Under Section 24(1) of the SEBI Act, 1992, if any person contravenes or attempts to contravene or abets the contravention of the provisions of this Act or of any rules or regulations made thereunder, what criminal punishment can be imposed by a Court of competent jurisdiction?
options: Imprisonment for a term which may extend to ten years, or with fine, which may extend to twenty-five crore rupees, or with both.
Imprisonment up to 3 years and fine up to ₹1 Crore.
Imprisonment up to 1 year and fine up to ₹50 Lakhs.
Strictly monetary fine with zero provision for imprisonment.
ref: Section 24(1) of the Securities and Exchange Board of India Act, 1992
explanation: Under Section 24(1), without prejudice to any award of penalty by the adjudicating officer under this Act, if any person contravenes or attempts to contravene or abets the contravention of the provisions of this Act or of any rules or regulations made thereunder, he shall be punishable with imprisonment for a term which may extend to ten years, or with fine, which may extend to twenty-five crore rupees or with both.
